current_interpretation: For each FY2025 measurement, the draft requires exactly one applicable numeric limit. It pairs measurements to permit limits by matching LIMIT_VALUE_ID and LIMIT_SET_SCHEDULE_ID from the DMR row to permit_limits.csv, and it only includes measurements whose monitoring period end falls within the FY2025 window (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30). The join produced one measurement_limit_pair per FY2025 measurement (824 pairs), so the uniqueness requirement is currently satisfied on this fixture.
status: requirement authored; currently satisfied on this fixture
why_it_matters: Purpose A needs a single enforceable numeric limit per measurement to decide whether a reported value exceeds the applicable limit. If more than one limit could govern the same measurement, compliance comparison is ambiguous unless the analysis can rank or collapse candidates.
supporting_evidence_used: ISSUES.md relation counts: dmr_measurement 824 rows, measurement_limit_pair 824 rows, numeric_comparison_candidate 342 rows
evidence_snippets_used: LIMIT_BEGIN_DATE, LIMIT_END_DATE, LIMIT_VALUE_ID, LIMIT_SET_SCHEDULE_ID from permit_limits.csv
contracts_involved: world.derive(measurement_limit_pair, join on LIMIT_VALUE_ID and LIMIT_SET_SCHEDULE_ID)
world.derive(fy2025_measurement, filtered by interval_contains on monitoring_period_end)
alternatives_considered: Treat overlapping or staged limit intervals as separate governing limits rather than forcing cardinality ONE
Treat catalog restatements of the same limit (distinct LIMIT_VALUE_ID or LIMIT_SET_SCHEDULE_ID rows) as multiple applicable limits rather than one
Derive applicable limit by intersecting monitoring period with limit begin/end dates instead of relying on the DMR row's embedded limit keys alone
affected_computations: numeric_comparison_candidate (342 rows, subset with both reported and limit numeric values)
remaining_uncertainty: Whether overlapping or staged interval rows should remain separate identities rather than being forced to a single governing limit; whether catalog restatements of the same limit should count as multiples.
